/// <summary>UX slice 4: an internal bridge error as a person reads it. Line = plain sentence (web-words.md "When Sentinel is not
/// connected"); Detail = status, technical cause and the bridge's own detail for a "Details" fold, "" when none. An error that is
/// not a bridge/connection one comes back unchanged (Detail ""). Pure; the internal "Bridge <code>:" value is never altered.</summary>
public static (string Line, string Detail) Plain(string err)
if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(err)) return ("Sentinel could not answer.", "");
var m = System.Text.RegularExpressions.Regex.Match(err, @"^Bridge (\d{3}): (.*)$", System.Text.RegularExpressions.RegexOptions.Singleline);
if (m.Success)
var code = m.Groups[1].Value; var rest = m.Groups[2].Value; var extra = "";
var i = rest.IndexOf(DetailMark, StringComparison.Ordinal);
if (i >= 0) { extra = rest.Substring(i + DetailMark.Length); rest = rest.Substring(0, i); }
var http = "HTTP " + code + (extra.Length > 0 ? " Â· " + extra : "");
return code switch
"401" => ("Your sign-in was not accepted. Sign in again.", http + (rest.Length > 0 ? " Â· " + rest : "")),
"403" => ("You do not have permission for this.", http + (rest.Length > 0 ? " Â· " + rest : "")),
_ when code.StartsWith("5") => ("Sentinel could not answer.", http + (rest.Length > 0 ? " Â· " + rest : "")),
_ => (rest.Length > 0 ? rest : "Sentinel refused this.", http),
if (err.StartsWith("the bridge did not answer", StringComparison.Ordinal) || err.StartsWith("the connection failed", StringComparison.Ordinal))
return ("Sentinel is not connected.", err);
return (err, "");

new: Some actions, such as installing a catalogue on the office, require you to be signed in as yourself because Sentinel checks your role.

old: This PC must have the sign-in address and key (Standards ▸ PC Settings).
new: This PC must have the sign-in address and key (More ▸ PC Settings).

new: The Sentinel service address in the configuration must be one Sentinel accepts; if it is refused the dialog shows the reason.

old: Click Sentinel > Standards > Sign in.
new: Click Sentinel > More > Sign in.

old: On success the top line reads "Signed in as <your e-mail> - the ledger records your e-mail." Click Close.
new: On success the top line reads "Signed in as <your e-mail> - History records your e-mail." Click Close.

new: Your session is stored on this PC and used for every thing you send from Revit; History entries show your e-mail.

old: Before signing in the top line reads either "Signed out - governed calls are refused until you sign in" or "Signed out - this PC's shared machine token is used, and the ledger records ...
new: Before signing in the top line reads either "Signed out - nothing can be sent from Revit until you sign in" or "Signed out - this PC's shared access is used, and History records ...

old: If a stored session can no longer be refreshed, Sentinel signs you out and asks you to use Standards > Sign in again.
new: If a stored session can no longer be refreshed, Sentinel signs you out and asks you to use More > Sign in again.

old: The dialog's footer shows which address it signs in at and which bridge it uses.
new: The dialog's footer shows which address it signs in at and which Sentinel it uses.

old: Set this PC's own Sentinel settings in a window — the bridge, the sign-in, the local AI and Ghost Builder's folders — and test each connection.
new: Set this PC's own Sentinel settings in a window — the connection and sign-in, the local AI and Ghost Builder's folders — and test each connection.

new: Some settings belong to a PC, not to a project: where this PC finds Sentinel, how it signs in, which local AI model it uses and where Ghost Builder finds its family library and layer mapping file.

old: This PC's shared token and the sign-in key are never shown: the window only says whether one is set.
new: This PC's shared access code and the sign-in key are never shown: the window only says whether one is set.

old: Bridge address
new: Sentinel service address

old: Where this PC finds the Sentinel bridge.
new: Where this PC finds Sentinel.

old: On the PC that runs the bridge it is http://localhost:4100; elsewhere an https address.
new: On the PC that runs Sentinel it is http://localhost:4100; elsewhere an https address.

old: Test says whether a bridge answers.
new: Test says whether a Sentinel answers.

old: This PC's shared token
new: This PC's shared access code

old: The bridge's machine credential.
new: Sentinel's machine credential.

old: It works only with the bridge on this PC; people elsewhere sign in instead.
new: It works only with Sentinel on this PC; people elsewhere sign in instead.

old: Read only: what the office or project lead set in the web app (Project settings ▸ AI privacy) for the open model's project.
new: Read only: what the office or project lead set in the web app (Settings ▸ Project ▸ AI privacy) for the open model's project.

old: Click Standards ▸ PC Settings under Sentinel > Standards & Build.
new: Click More ▸ PC Settings under Sentinel.

old: If Save is refused, the window says why in words — for example a plain http address on another PC, or a shared token with a bridge that is not on this PC.
new: If Save is refused, the window says why in words — for example a plain http address on another PC, or a shared access code with a Sentinel that is not on this PC.

old: The drawings folder Ghost Builder reads is set per model in Standards ▸ Project Setup.
new: The drawings folder Ghost Builder reads is set per model in More ▸ Project Setup.

old: An Issues window that is already open keeps the old bridge address until you open it again.
new: An Issues window that is already open keeps the old Sentinel service address until you open it again.

old: Reads the office standard out of the open "golden" model, lets you review and tick it, then builds it into this model and into the project's ruleset.
new: Reads the office standard out of the open "golden" model, lets you review and tick it, then builds it into this model and into the project's standards.

old: Building also installs the ticked worksets and naming rules into the web project's ruleset so the scanner enforces them.
new: Building also installs the ticked worksets and naming rules into the web project's standards so the scanner enforces them.

old: For the ruleset part of a build, the model must be bound to a web project (Project Setup); otherwise the model is built but the ruleset line says it was not installed because there is no project.
new: For the project standards part of a build, the model must be bound to a web project (Project Setup); otherwise the model is built but the project standards line says it was not installed because there is no project.

old: Install catalogue on office needs you signed in, a pack with a harvested catalogue, and a project that belongs to an office; the bridge checks that you are a lead on that office.
new: Install catalogue on office needs you signed in, a pack with a harvested catalogue, and a project that belongs to an office; Sentinel checks that you are a lead on that office.

old: Builds the ticked worksets, shared parameters, view templates and browser schemes into the model, and installs worksets and naming rules into the project's ruleset.
new: Builds the ticked worksets, shared parameters, view templates and browser schemes into the model, and installs worksets and naming rules into the project's standards.

old: Sends this pack's worksets, shared parameters, type catalogue and current ruleset to the web project's Documents > READINESS view so the office standard can be measured.
new: Sends this pack's worksets, shared parameters, type catalogue and current project standards to the web project's Documents ▸ Readiness view so the office standard can be measured.

old: Open the golden model or template and click Sentinel > Standards > Build Office System.
new: Open the golden model or template and click Sentinel > More > Build Office System.

old: Read the report in the window: created, skipped and failed items, followed by the "Ruleset install" outcome.
new: Read the report in the window: created, skipped and failed items, followed by the "Project standards install" outcome.

old: The window shows Created, Skipped and Failed lists, then the ruleset install result and a status line such as "Done - N created, N skipped, N failed".
new: The window shows Created, Skipped and Failed lists, then the project standards install result and a status line such as "Done - N created, N skipped, N failed".

old: When the model is bound and worksets or naming rules were ticked, the project's ruleset gains a new version containing them and the scanner reloads it.
new: When the model is bound and worksets or naming rules were ticked, the project's standards gain a new version containing them and the scanner reloads it.

old: If the project was inheriting the office's ruleset, it now has its own and stops inheriting later office changes (the window warns).
new: If the project was inheriting the office's project standards, it now has its own and stops inheriting later office changes (the window warns).

old: If Revit kept the build and something was created, one "Apply Standard" row is written to the project ledger.
new: If Revit kept the build and something was created, one "Apply Standard" row is written to the project's History.

old: A cached copy of the ruleset is never used as the base for an install: if the bridge did not answer, the model is built but the ruleset is not installed, and the report says to run Apply again when the bridge is up.
new: A cached copy of the project standards is never used as the base for an install: if Sentinel did not answer, the model is built but the project standards are not installed, and the report says to run Apply again when Sentinel is up.

old: The build is the same as in Build Office System: items that already exist are skipped, the whole build is one Undo entry, and ticked worksets and naming rules are installed into the web project's ruleset when the model is bound.
new: The build is the same as in Build Office System: items that already exist are skipped, the whole build is one Undo entry, and ticked worksets and naming rules are installed into the web project's standards when the model is bound.

old: For the ruleset install, the model must be bound to a web project (Project Setup); otherwise the model is still built and the report says no ruleset was installed.
new: For the project standards install, the model must be bound to a web project (Project Setup); otherwise the model is still built and the report says no project standards were installed.

old: Open or create the target model and bind it to its web project (Project Setup) if you want the ruleset installed.
new: Open or create the target model and bind it to its web project (Project Setup) if you want the project standards installed.

old: Click Sentinel > Standards > Apply Standard.
new: Click Sentinel > More > Apply Standard.

old: Click Build ticked items and read the Created, Skipped and Failed report and the ruleset install result.
new: Click Build ticked items and read the Created, Skipped and Failed report and the project standards install result.

old: The project's ruleset gets a new version with the pack's worksets and naming rules when the model is bound and the bridge answers.
new: The project's standards gets a new version with the pack's worksets and naming rules when the model is bound and Sentinel answers.

old: One "Apply Standard" row on the project ledger when Revit kept the build and something was created.
new: One "Apply Standard" row in the project's History when Revit kept the build and something was created.

old: Ticked worksets and naming rules also go into the web project's ruleset when you build.
new: Ticked worksets and naming rules also go into the web project's standards when you build.

old: To build the results into a model: the same requirements as Build Office System (bound to a web project for the ruleset install; workshared for worksets).
new: To build the results into a model: the same requirements as Build Office System (bound to a web project for the project standards install; workshared for worksets).

old: Click Sentinel > Standards > Ingest Docs.
new: Click Sentinel > More > Ingest Docs.

old: Click Build ticked items to create the worksets and shared parameters in the model and add the worksets and naming rules to the ruleset, or Save pack to keep the pack for Apply Standard.
new: Click Build ticked items to create the worksets and shared parameters in the model and add the worksets and naming rules to the project standards, or Save pack to keep the pack for Apply Standard.

old: On build: the same Created, Skipped and Failed report, one Undo entry, ruleset install and ledger row as the other standards tools.
new: On build: the same Created, Skipped and Failed report, one Undo entry, project standards install and History entry as the other standards tools.

old: Shows the web project's ledger counts for delivery gate runs, naming renames and family heals, and prices them if the project has an ROI standard.
new: Shows the web project's History counts for pre-publish check runs, naming renames and family heals, and prices them if the project has an ROI standard.

old: ROI Dashboard reads the open model's web project ledger and counts what Sentinel has done: delivery gate runs, naming renames and family heals.
new: ROI Dashboard reads the open model's web project History and counts what Sentinel has done: pre-publish check runs, naming renames and family heals.

old: It also counts fixes that write ledger rows (auto-fixes, fix-in-place values written, Doctor resolutions) but does not price them, and it lists what it cannot count, such as CDE intercepts, MEP voids, BCF export and clash views, because those write no ledger row.
new: It also counts fixes that write History entries (auto-fixes, fix-in-place values written, Doctor resolutions) but does not price them, and it lists what it cannot count, such as file-name stops, MEP voids, BCF export and clash views, because those write no History entry.

old: Every number is a count of ledger rows, so it reflects what happened on the web project, not just this model or session.
new: Every number is a count of History entries, so it reflects what happened on the web project, not just this model or session.

old: The Sentinel bridge must be reachable.
new: Sentinel must be reachable.

old: Click Sentinel > Standards & Build > ROI Dashboard.
new: Click Sentinel > More > ROI Dashboard.

old: Revit pauses briefly while the ledger is read, then the "Return on investment" window opens.
new: Revit pauses briefly while History is read, then the "Return on investment" window opens.

old: A window headed "Return on investment" whose first line states the project and how many ledger rows were read (and if only the newest were read because the ledger holds more).
new: A window headed "Return on investment" whose first line states the project and how many History entries were read (and if only the newest were read because History holds more).

old: Lines for: Delivery gate runs, Naming renames, Family heals (each with minutes and amount if priced), Money (total, currency and hourly rate, or why it is not shown), Fixes on the ledger (not priced), and Not counted.
new: Lines for: Pre-publish check runs, Naming renames, Family heals (each with minutes and amount if priced), Money (total, currency and hourly rate, or why it is not shown), Fixes in History (not priced), and Not counted.

old: Nothing is written to the model or the ledger.
new: Nothing is written to the model or History.

old: If the ledger is large, only the newest rows are counted and the header says so.
new: If History is large, only the newest rows are counted and the header says so.

old: The Model from Drawings pulldown groups the seven tools that take a project from drawings or photos to a governed Revit model, in the order they are meant to be run.
new: The Build pulldown groups the seven tools that take a project from drawings or photos to a checked Revit model, in the order they are meant to be run.

old: Model from Drawings is a pulldown, not a command of its own.
new: Build is a pulldown, not a command of its own.

old: How the tools are governed: Datum and Ghost Builder show you a review window and write only what you tick.
new: How the tools are checked: Datum and Ghost Builder show you a review window and write only what you tick.

old: Photo Massing, Shell a Mass and Promote (DD) do not write to the model themselves; they file their proposal as a changeset on the project's web ledger and open Review AI Proposals, where a person ticks and applies it.
new: Photo Massing, Shell a Mass and Promote (DD) do not write to the model themselves; they send their proposal as a set of proposed changes for review in the project's History and open Review AI Proposals, where a person ticks and applies it.

old: For the changeset-based tools (Photo Massing, Shell a Mass, Promote (DD)) the model must be bound to a web project: use Project Setup first.
new: For the tools that send proposed changes (Photo Massing, Shell a Mass, Promote (DD)) the model must be bound to a web project: use Project Setup first.

old: The Sentinel bridge must be running for the tools that file changesets or read the standards.
new: Sentinel must be running for the tools that send sets of proposed changes or read the standards.

old: Open the Sentinel tab and the Model from Drawings pulldown.
new: Open the Sentinel tab and the Build pulldown.

old: Photo Massing, Shell a Mass and Promote (DD) put changesets into Review AI Proposals; nothing is placed until a person applies them.
new: Photo Massing, Shell a Mass and Promote (DD) put sets of proposed changes into Review AI Proposals; nothing is placed until a person applies them.

old: Elements Sentinel places or changes carry a provenance stamp (source, source file, layer, rule, approver, ledger row, time).
new: Elements Sentinel places or changes carry a provenance stamp (source, source file, layer, rule, approver, History entry, time).

old: Revit sometimes empties its Undo list afterwards; the tool's dialog and the ledger row then tell you what was made.
new: Revit sometimes empties its Undo list afterwards; the tool's dialog and the History entry then tell you what was made.

old: When the run creates something, it also sends a datum row and a build receipt to the project's ledger.
new: When the run creates something, it also sends a datum row and a build receipt to the project's History.

old: Open the project and click Model from Drawings, then "1 · Datum from Drawings".
new: Open the project and click Build, then "1 · Datum from Drawings".

old: One datum row and one build receipt are sent to the project's ledger (the pane's log says what the ledger answered).
new: One datum row and one build receipt are sent to the project's History (the pane's log says what History answered).

old: When you press "Build ticked layers ▶" the build is filed on the project's ledger as changesets from the drawing and placed in one step, with every element stamped with its source drawing and checksum.
new: When you press "Build ticked layers ▶" the build is recorded in the project's History as sets of proposed changes from the drawing and placed in one step, with every element stamped with its source drawing and checksum.

old: A model not bound to a project runs the build as a local changeset with no ledger.
new: A model not bound to a project runs the build as a local set of proposed changes with no History.

old: Click Model from Drawings, then "2 · Ghost Builder".
new: Click Build, then "2 · Ghost Builder".

old: The summary names the standards used, how many elements were placed, how walls were typed (by the guideline, by the layer mapping, by you, or left as a gap), what was skipped and why, any types or families added, Revit warnings and the ledger line.
new: The summary names the standards used, how many elements were placed, how walls were typed (by the guideline, by the layer mapping, by you, or left as a gap), what was skipped and why, any types or families added, Revit warnings and the History line.

old: The build is also filed as changesets with source dwg on the project's ledger.
new: The build is also recorded as sets of proposed changes with source dwg in the project's History.

new: That sends one set of proposed changes for review (recorded in the project's History) containing the Building Story levels the mass needs that the model lacks and one untyped mass between them.

old: Review AI Proposals opens on the changeset and a person applies it there.
new: Review AI Proposals opens on the proposed changes, and a person applies them there.

old: Photos in the project's evidence pack that have been admitted and blurred (Files ▸ Evidence in the web app).
new: Photos in the project's evidence pack that have been admitted and blurred (Documents ▸ Files in the web app).

old: The Sentinel bridge running, so the evidence pack can be read and the changeset filed.
new: Sentinel running, so the evidence pack can be read and the proposed changes sent.

new: Open a plan view of the model and click Build, then "2b · Photo Massing".

new: One set of proposed changes with the missing Building Story levels and a mass is recorded in the project's History.

new: A receipt for the vision run is sent to History.

old: If a Photo Massing changeset is already waiting, that one opens instead of a second being filed.
new: If a Photo Massing set of proposed changes is already waiting, that one opens instead of a second being sent.

new: An older Photo Massing set of proposed changes that was read outside the evidence pack must be declined in Review AI Proposals before you run it again.

old: Turns a selected mass into typed walls, a floor per level and a flat roof, one storey at a time, filed for review as changesets.
new: Turns a selected mass into typed walls, a floor per level and a flat roof, one storey at a time, sent for review as sets of proposed changes.

old: Yes files it; No is a read-only run that changes nothing.
new: Yes sends it; No is a read-only run that changes nothing.

old: A mass in the model: an in-place mass, a mass family, a mass made as a direct shape, or the mass from Photo Massing once its changeset has been applied.
new: A mass in the model: an in-place mass, a mass family, a mass made as a direct shape, or the mass from Photo Massing once its set of proposed changes has been applied.

old: The Sentinel bridge running.
new: Sentinel running.

old: Yes files the shell for review.
new: Yes sends the shell for review.

old: Click Model from Drawings, then "2c · Shell a Mass".
new: Click Build, then "2c · Shell a Mass".

old: Wait while the bridge is read in the background.
new: Wait while Sentinel is answers in the background.

new: Press Yes to file, or No to stop with nothing sent.

old: Review AI Proposals opens on the first changeset.
new: Review AI Proposals opens on the first set of proposed changes.

old: One changeset up to 200 elements (one review, one Undo), or one changeset per storey above that.
new: One set of proposed changes up to 200 elements (one review, one Undo), or one set of proposed changes per storey above that.

old: A receipt for the planning is sent to the ledger.
new: A receipt for the planning is sent to History.

old: Rows sent to a person ride on the first changeset filed.
new: Rows sent to a person ride on the first set of proposed changes sent.

new: If a Promote or Shell set of proposed changes is still waiting for review, it opens instead; apply or decline it, then run Shell a Mass again.

old: If only some storey changesets were filed, decline them and run it again.
new: If only some storey sets of proposed changes were sent, decline them and run it again.

old: If the mass cannot be shelled, the dialog says why and nothing is planned or filed.
new: If the mass cannot be shelled, the dialog says why and nothing is planned or sent.

new: The project's standards must be loaded: run Scan Now once, otherwise the tool refuses because it cannot judge the view names.

new: Click Build, then "3 · Annotate Views".

new: One annotate row goes to History naming the views and datums the model holds.

new: If Edit ▸ Undo does not list Annotate views, the History entry is the record of which views to delete and which datums to unpin by hand.

old: Yes files the plan; No is a read-only run.
new: Yes sends the plan; No is a read-only run.

old: Filing creates one changeset per storey on the project's ledger, and Review AI Proposals opens on the first.

new: Nothing is written to the model until a person ticks the elements and applies the proposed changes.

new: No type is ever created, each change is stamped, and an Undo of it is recorded in History.

old: The Sentinel bridge running; otherwise you get "Couldn't reach the bridge".
new: Sentinel running; otherwise you get "Couldn't reach Sentinel".

old: Yes files one changeset per storey.
new: Yes sends one set of proposed changes per storey.

new: No is a read-only run: nothing is sent, but the LOD state and type-gap rows are still sent to History.

old: Click Model from Drawings, then "4 · Promote (DD)".
new: Click Build, then "4 · Promote (DD)".

old: Revit stays usable while the bridge is read.
new: Revit stays usable while Sentinel answers.

new: A storey whose every change was declined in an earlier review is not sent again.

old: Changesets, one per storey, on the project's ledger and opened for review.
new: Sets of proposed changes, one per storey, in the project's History and opened for review.

new: History entries for the LOD state now, the type gaps, the foreign types and a run receipt.

new: If a previous Promote or Shell set of proposed changes is still waiting, it opens instead of a new plan.

new: If the model is re-bound to another project during the run, nothing is sent; run Promote again.

new: The dialog names the element (category, id and name) and then says whether Sentinel placed or changed it, the source, the checksum (sha256) of the source file, the CAD layer, the rule that typed it, the approver, the History entry of the proposal and the time.

new: Click Build, then "5 · Provenance".

new: Choose what no set of proposed changes may edit — grids, levels, structure and chosen worksets — for this project or the whole office.

old: The model is bound to its web project (Standards ▸ Project Setup).
new: The model is bound to its web project (More ▸ Project Setup).

new: Click Protection under Sentinel > More.

new: A new version of the protection policy on the project or its office, with a History entry naming who saved it.

new: Click More ▸ Modelling Guideline under Sentinel.

old: The window names the version saved; it is recorded in the ledger.
new: The window names the version saved; it is recorded in History.

old: A new version of the guideline on the project or its office, with a ledger row naming who saved it.
new: A new version of the guideline on the project or its office, with a History entry naming who saved it.

new: In the web app, Settings ▸ Project ▸ Standards in force names this window on the guideline row.

new: Publish model hands it to Revit's IFC exporter for every export.

new: Click More ▸ IFC Export Mapping under Sentinel.

new: A new version of the IFC export mapping on the project or its office, with a History entry naming who saved it.

new: The next Publish model uses it.
